bullets.text: Q3 CR of 94.2 paired with 5% premium growth contributed to Progressive's positioning within a 'zone of healthy operating combinations'; quarter and YTD results both exceeded the 96 combined ratio threshold objective.

Double-digit new application growth achieved across both channels in the quarter's final month; Direct maintained double-digit gains against 2011; build in retention and Net Promoter Score remains necessary for PIF growth.

Florida auto changes were extremely productive, resulting in meaningful growth and continued strong margins; rates are expected to stay competitive longer than originally planned, while normal state-by-state adjustments remain small to stay nimble.

Snapshot will factor into rating over $2B of 2013 private passenger NPW, with profitability targets well in-hand; secured four IP licenses for 2015; agent-offer rates remain opportunities for greater penetration.
Net income fell 16% to $232M, due in part to realized gain timing differences; YTD portfolio total return rebounded to 3.5%; repurchased $54M of 6.70% debentures and retired $150M of maturing debt.

Branding introduced an added dimension answering 'what kind of company would Flo work for?' to cultivate trust; media exposure will be lower frequency and expected to be longer lived, complementing product advertising.

Current auto product design represents the majority of countrywide offerings; preferred and multi-product bundled households are faster-growing segments; largest of eleven homeowners partners announced an ownership change without anticipated relationship impact.

Prior loss cost projections exceeded actualized trends by approximately one percentage point over the predicted timeframe; Special Lines experienced lower losses alongside decreased riding days and softer motorcycle insurance demand.

Premium grew 5%; exceeding the 96 combined ratio threshold objective fuels management's desire to grow as fast as possible; Commercial Lines experienced relatively slow growth, with efforts on ensuring profitability deemed well placed.

Claims opened three Service Centers, reaching 61 locations, with two more planned; implemented center changes meet performance expectations, supporting expansion under the decade-old 'Cars not Cash' physical damage strategy.
